newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-H&M 95/96 profit to rise 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-H&M 95/96 profit to rise 40 pct.

text.p: Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz (H&M) was expected to report a pre-tax profit of 1.85 billion crowns for the 12 months to November 30, 1996, against 1.32 billion a year ago, a Reuters poll found.
Forecasts from 14 analysts ranged between 1.68 billion and 2.00 billion crowns.
The company was expected to propose a dividend of 9.30 crowns for 1995/96 compared to 7.75 crowns a year earlier.
H&M's pre-tax profit was forecast to rise further in 1996/97 with an average forecast of 2.28 billion crowns. Forecasts varied between 2.10 billion and 2.46 billion crowns.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Enskilda, Fiba, Goldman Sachs, James Capel, Handelsbanken, Kleinwort Benson, Matteus, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Grenfell, Nordiska, Penser, SBC Warburg, and Swedbank.
H&M was due to publish its results early afternoon on January 30.
